content: The test image shows a corn leaf with numerous small, scattered reddish-brown to tan lesions across the surface. Some appear as small raised spots/pustules, others as irregular patches. This pattern is consistent with rust or Physoderma brown spot. Let me compare reference images.

**Analysis:**

The test image shows a corn leaf with:
- Numerous small (~1-3mm) reddish-brown to tan scattered lesions
- Some larger irregular coalesced tan/brown patches
- Lesions distributed across the leaf surface (midrib visible at top)
- Spots appear somewhat raised/pustular, reddish-brown coloration

**Comparison with references:**

- **Southern rust**: Bright orange, very small, densely packed circular pustules — test image has more reddish-brown/tan coloration and larger irregular patches
- **Common rust**: Larger oval/elongated reddish-brown pustules, can age to darker coloration with irregular patches — the bottom-right panel of the Common rust reference shows many scattered small dark spots with irregular tan patches, matching the test image closely
- **Physoderma brown spot**: Dark spots arranged in bands near midrib — the banding pattern is absent in the test image

The test image most closely matches **Common rust** — the mix of small reddish-brown lesions and larger coalesced tan patches, along with the darker (rather than bright orange) coloration, aligns better with Common rust at various stages than with Southern rust.
